solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Marijuana's turning up in bar

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something up means reading it from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: pot is slang for marijuana, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone notices cannabis being smoked in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to prevent or halt it, a verb synonym of the answer.

clue.text: High Street I visited at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: standard abbreviation in addresses
the Roman numeral I is one
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the main shopping street they finally went to.
explanation.walkthrough: High looks like part of High Street, but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being high and being stoned are both slang for intoxication by drugs.

clue.text: Callas, say, Greek character who performs music

definitions.note: a noun phrase: one who performs music

blocks.note: the opera singer Maria Callas is one example of a Maria
a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Maria Callas is praised as a diva who performs music.
explanation.walkthrough: Callas looks like the subject, but 'say' marks her as just one example of someone with that first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariachi is a Mexican street musician who plays in a small band, hence one who performs music.

clue.text: Material turned over to protect cold ground

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped, so its letters run the other way
to protect something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: a cotton fabric
C for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Fabric is folded over to shield the cold earth.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversed denim gives MINED, which wraps around C to make MINCED.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground meat is minced meat: both mean chopped finely, a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: Get rid of stylish rug, offered with reduction

indicators.note: the words are reduced, trimmed at both ends, leaving a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the end of the first word to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A seller disposes of a fashionable rug by putting it on sale at a discount.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug off a cold or a worry is to throw it off, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: A net closed round young person

indicators.note: bringing letters round means turning them about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A youngster is trapped as a net is drawn tight around them.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, someone between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Street art regularly featured a fish

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every second letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mural in the street often included a picture of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small brightly coloured tropical fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Went away round river with a coat on

indicators.note: one word goes round another, enclosing it

blocks.note: disappeared
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone walked off by the river, wearing their coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The coat is not clothing but a layer of glossy finish, as on wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Something varnished has been given a protective coat of clear lacquer.

clue.text: Sid's band? It gets continually worse

blocks.note: Sid Vicious of the Sex Pistols; his band, playfully, is his circle
a chain of events where each problem feeds the next

explanation.walkthrough: Sid Vicious was the punk bassist of the Sex Pistols; a circle is a ring or band, so his band is whimsically his circle. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicious circle is a self-reinforcing cycle in which each bad outcome makes things deteriorate further.

clue.text: Your violent struggles with a resistance agitator

indicators.note: things that struggle thrash about, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written for the rearrangement
taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Your fierce fights with the underground resistance mark you as a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolutionary is someone who stirs up and campaigns for political overthrow, an agitator.

clue.text: Chief changes caption

indicators.note: the word is changed into a different arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The editor-in-chief rewrites the caption under a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Chief reads as a newspaper boss, but the definition is a Native American leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiac was an eighteenth-century Ottawa war leader who led a rebellion against British rule.

clue.text: Food created using a computer's recipe is third rate

indicators.note: the 's ... is phrasing says one letter in the word now is something else, a swap

blocks.note: simulated by computer
R (from Latin recipe, take) heads prescriptions
C is a third-class grade, after A and B

explanation.surface: A dish generated by computer software turns out to have a mediocre recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as has: the computer word's R becomes C. R is the old abbreviation for recipe, meaning take, on prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Victual is an old word for provisions or nourishment, usually seen in the plural victuals.

clue.text: Conservative beginning to offend Liberal Democrat on train

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter
abbreviation for the UK party
to train is to school, as in schooling a horse

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is careful not to upset a Lib Dem rival on the train.
explanation.walkthrough: Train looks like a railway carriage, but it is the verb to educate. The Liberal Democrats are a UK political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Old school describes traditional, old-fashioned attitudes, which is what conservative means with a small c.

clue.text: Eliminate rising body odour, before long and repeat

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up, so backwards

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
L for long, as in clothing sizes
to iterate is to do again

explanation.surface: Instructions for getting rid of persistent body odour: keep washing and do it again.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out completely, a strong synonym for eliminating.

clue.text: Refuse to take king into bed

indicators.note: the outer word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: a doss is a makeshift place to sleep
R for rex, Latin king

explanation.surface: A queen declines to let the king into her bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse looks like a verb; here it is the noun meaning rubbish. Doss is British slang for a rough bed or sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste matter, the same as rubbish or refuse.

clue.text: Women receiving diamonds from young men

indicators.note: one word receives another, holding it inside

blocks.note: polite word for women
D for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: Women are given diamond jewellery by their young admirers.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddies is a Scottish, affectionate word for lads or boys, so young men.

clue.text: In action, explosive bomb is discharged

indicators.note: one piece is put in another, sitting inside it
an explosion scatters things, so the letters are blown into a new order

blocks.note: a deed is an act
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: During combat, a bomb goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: Discharged suggests the bomb firing, but it means released from military service.
explanation.definitionFit: To be demobbed is to be demobilised, formally released from the armed forces.

clue.text: Fretful about fungus

indicators.note: about means turned around or moved about, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle is an edible underground fungus prized in cooking.

clue.text: E.g. beer brewed in this country by extreme enthusiast

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred up
one piece sits in the other

blocks.note: for a British setter, this country is the UK
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Beer brewed at home by an obsessive hobbyist.
explanation.walkthrough: E.g. is part of the letters, not an example marker.
explanation.definitionFit: An übergeek is a super-geek, someone with an extreme obsessive interest in a specialist subject.

clue.text: Publication reported about legendary misanthrope

indicators.note: something reported is spoken aloud, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: Time is a news magazine and on means about

explanation.surface: A newspaper story concerns a famously people-hating figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens, subject of Shakespeare's play, was a legendary man who came to hate humankind.

clue.text: Observe water in liquid form, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: to see or spot
second, cryptic meaning: water that is not frozen

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOT ICE: liquid water is water that is not ice. The 'perhaps' warns of the wordplay reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to observe or perceive it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Strong suspicion, when voiced, is resolved

indicators.note: a thing voiced is said out loud, so its sound is what counts

blocks.note: iron for strong, doubt for suspicion

explanation.surface: A firmly held suspicion, once spoken, is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Problems that are ironed out are smoothed away and settled, an idiom for resolved.

clue.text: Southern Indian expanses?

blocks.note: surface reading: wide tracts of land in the south of India
setter's reading: two great bodies of water named Southern and Indian

explanation.walkthrough: Southern Indian looks like a region of India; read separately, each word names one of the world's great seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Southern and Indian are both named major marine bodies, vast expanses of salt water.

clue.text: Automatic rifle – 19 edges away

indicators.note: with the edges taken away, a word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: to rifle through is to ransack or steal
the answer to clue 19

explanation.surface: A rifle that fires automatically, with clue 19's ends cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Rifle looks like a gun, completing automatic rifle, but it is the verb to rob. The 19 answer loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic means mechanical and done without thought, like a machine acting automatically.

clue.text: Capital city is large, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be another arrangement of themselves

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A capital city is probably a big place.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital of Algeria, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Grain yield reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: to cede is to yield or give up

explanation.surface: A farmer's grain harvest figures are announced.
explanation.walkthrough: Yield suggests a crop harvest, but it is the verb to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a single seed of a cereal plant, such as a kernel of wheat.

clue.text: Go to restrain educator blowing top, showing lack of loyalty

indicators.note: losing its top, the word drops its first letter
to restrain is to hold in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a go is an attempt
one who educates

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hold back a furious teacher who has lost their temper, betraying them.
explanation.walkthrough: Blowing top looks like losing one's temper, but it means the word loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal of trust, the very absence of loyalty.

clue.text: Wise, perhaps, some consider Nietzche

indicators.note: some means a portion, taken from inside the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Some people regard the philosopher Nietzsche as wise.
explanation.walkthrough: Wise is not an adjective but a surname: Ernie Wise was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedian Ernie Wise is an example of a person named Ernie, a first-name relation.
